title: Related Questions
question: Related Questions Q. I will go for Hajj in-shaAllah. I will stay in 'Azizia’ from 5 September until September 22. Will I be a musafir or not, knowing that I also leave to Mina and Muzdalifah? 2189 views Q. Performing Umrah with Mehram/husband. 6379 views Q. We are going for Umrah in Ramadan, in-shaAllah and would like to ask you two questions 2374 views Q. I live in Jeddah with my wife. We went to perform Umra. We completed the Tawaf and Saee. After that, my wife wanted to cut her hair herself but I told her that only someone who has already got Halaqa can cut your hair. She waited for me so I can get my haircut and then cut her hair. After I had my Haircut, we discovered we did not have a scissors to cut her hair. We thought we can go home (Jeddah) and do that. Once we returned home, we kissed each other. Immediately after, she remembered that she needed to cut her hair. Now, please advise us if we should give any "Dum" having done this? If so, what should it be? and can we give Dum back in Pakistan where people need it the most? 9977 views Q. I went to Makkah from Jeddah and performed umrah alone. The next day I took my family to Jurana from Makkah without the intention of performing Umrah myself. My family performed umrah on returnin to makkah mukarima and i didnot. Is Dumh due on me or not? 2271 views Q. One of my friends tells me that doing an umrah by wearing ahram from "masjid-e-Aisha" is permissible only for women folk and not for men. His explanation was that Nabi-e-Kareem Muhammad (Pbuh) asked aisha(radiallahu anha) to do umrah from "masjid-e-aisha" as she was sick during the time of Hajj, and her brother was not asked to do the same when he accompanied her. If this was permissible for men then Nabi-e-Kareem Muhammad (Pbuh)would have also asked him to do umrah from "masjid-e-aisha". My friend also tells me that according to Imam Abu Hanifa Rahmatulla alayh, such umrah is permissible for men but is makruh. Please quote to the exact hadith in discussion and explanation as to how and why it is permissible for men and also comment on the views of my friend. Jazakallahukhaira. 4361 views Q. answer: Prayers & Duties >> Hajj & Umrah Question ID: 38252 Country: India Title: Should hajj badal be performed only by the person who has completed his hajj or the person who has not completed his hajj Question: Should hajj badal be performed only by the person who has completed his hajj or the person who has not completed his hajj? A person has enough wealth (jewel of 70000 and own house but what he earn is enough for his living and two portion of shop for rent in his home) to perform hajj but he did not complete his hajj. Can he go for hajj-e-badal? Answer ID: 38252 Posted on: Sep 1, 2020 Bismillah hir-Rahman nir-Rahim ! (Fatwa: 777/656/B=1433) It is better to send such person for hajj badal who has already performed his fardh hajj. It is makrooh to send a person who has not performed his fardh hajj, though the hajj shall be valid. A person who can afford his hajj he should not go for hajj badal rather he should perform his own hajj first. Allah (Subhana Wa Ta'ala) knows Best Darul Ifta, Darul Uloom Deoband, India
